title: Taming Transformer Without Using Learning Rate Warmup
comment: This paper is published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025
abstract:
Scaling Transformer to a large scale without using some technical tricks such as learning rate warump and using an obviously lower learning rate is an extremely challenging task, and is increasingly gaining more attention. In this paper, we provide a theoretical analysis for the process of training Transformer and reveal the rationale behind the model crash phenomenon in the training process, termed 	extit{spectral energy concentration} of ${ W_q}^{	op}  W_k$, which is the reason for a malignant entropy collapse, where ${ W_q}$ and $ W_k$ are the projection matrices for the query and the key in Transformer, respectively. To remedy this problem, motivated by 	extit{Weyl's Inequality}, we present a novel optimization strategy, \ie, making the weight updating in successive steps smooth -- if the ratio $ rac{σ_{1}(
abla  W_t)}{σ_{1}( W_{t-1})}$ is larger than a threshold, we will automatically bound the learning rate to a weighted multiple of $ rac{σ_{1}( W_{t-1})}{σ_{1}(
abla  W_t)}$, where $
abla  W_t$ is the updating quantity in step $t$. Such an optimization strategy can prevent spectral energy concentration to only a few directions, and thus can avoid malignant entropy collapse which will trigger the model crash. We conduct extensive experiments using ViT, Swin-Transformer and GPT, showing that our optimization strategy can effectively and stably train these Transformers without using learning rate warmup.
